title: Postural Changes During Right Heart Catheterization
brief_summary: Hemodynamic measurements obtained during pulmonary artery catheterization are essential for the diagnosis and classification of pulmonary hypertension. Traditionally, right heart catheterization (RHC) is done in the supine position. Cardiac output is known to change significantly based on position, due to the effects of gravity on venous return. There has not been a systematic investigation into these postural effects on pulmonary arterial pressures nor their effect on the diagnosis of pulmonary hypertension. It is our intent to study the differences in measurements obtained during RHC when the patient is supine, seated, and standing.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* All patients that are 18 years or older regardless of gender or race,
* are referred for RHC for evaluation of possible Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH)
* provide informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Inability to obtain pulmonary artery pressure or PCWP
study_population: The study population will be a cohort of patients referred for right heart catheterization for workup of pulmonary arterial hypertension.
condition: Right Heart Failure Due to Pulmonary Hypertension
